To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Tsc2(GFP1)CKO mouse models exhibit more severe epilepsy than Tsc1(GFP1) CKO mice and that the difference in severity may be related to mTOR activation.
Tsc2(Gfap-Cre) mice have a more severe epilepsy and neuropathology than Tsc1(Gfap-CRE) mice and this difference is correlated with the degree of mTOR activation.
Tsc2(GFP1)CKO, but not Tsc1(GFP1)KO mice, have higher levels of mTOR activation and that this difference is correlated with a more severe neurological and histological phenotype in Tsc2 mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of epilepsy in a mouse model.
the development of a new model for TSC, which is a disease that is characterized by the development of benign tumors and severe neurological manifestations.
understanding the mechanisms underlying the more severe neurological symptoms associated with TSC2 mutations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the severity of the epilepsy phenotype in mouse models is dependent upon the degree to which the mTOR pathway is activated.
the Tsc2 mutation in this study caused a more severe neurological disease than the Tsc1 mutation in a mouse model.
Tsc2(GFP1)CKO mouse model has a more severe neurological phenotypes than Tsc1(GFP1) CKO mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Tsc2(GFP)CKO mice are a more severe epilepsy model than Tsc1(GFP)CKOs, which may be a result of the higher mTOR activation in the Tsc2(GPF)CKO mice.
the severity of epilepsy and the histopathology in Tsc2 mice were more severe than Tsc1.

the Tsc2(Gfap1)CKO mouse model exhibits an earlier onset, higher frequency and more severe neurological phenotype, compared with the Tsc1(Gfap1)-CKO mouse model, which may be due to higher levels of mammalanian target of rapamaycin (mTOR) signaling in the Tsc2 model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Tsc2(GFP)CKO mouse model is more suitable for studying the pathophysiology of TSC and for testing novel therapeutic interventions than Tsc1(GFP)CKOs.
TSC2 is more critical than TSC1 for normal brain development and function.
